title: skills(objectstack-ai): teach `mcpPrompt` where SKILL.md explains which skills MCP offers as prompts
body:
domain:server#7 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibzuZJBQY4wUQFJbkfx

Filing gate: ① a teaching gap a merged change will open (follow-up of #34167 / PR #34236, Skills-docs owed). ⛔ Not a claim; triage sets the lane (expected `domain:skills`) and grade.
Business reason: an author who writes a skill only for the in-product agents reads `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` to learn which skills an MCP client is offered. Once PR #34236 lands, that page gives the wrong rule twice. It never names the opt-out, so the author cannot keep an in-product playbook away from Claude Code or Cursor. And it says the stdio transport "lists every skill", so the author expects an opted-out skill to show up there too.

## What is stale once PR #34236 merges

`skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` (≈ lines 380–388 on `main`), the paragraph that begins "`tools` binds nothing there but is read: `registerSkillPrompts` offers a skill on `prompts/list` / `prompts/get` only when …":

1. It does not name `SkillSchema.mcpPrompt`. `mcpPrompt: false` withholds a skill from `prompts/list` and `prompts/get` on every MCP connection, whatever its `tools` binding.
2. "the plugin's own stdio transport lists every skill" becomes false for `mcpPrompt: false` rows. Stdio withholds them too; the binding filter still does not apply there.

## Done when

- The paragraph names `mcpPrompt` (optional; `false` = in-product only, never offered over MCP; absent or `true` = today's binding rule), and the stdio sentence states the exception.
- The same wording reaches any mirror the skills gates require.
- It waits on PR #34236 merging. Until then the key does not exist on `main`.

Blocked-by: #34167
Dedupe words: `mcpPrompt SKILL.md`, `skill prompt opt-out skills doc`, `registerSkillPrompts paragraph`.
